source_text:
Περιπατοῦντός μου εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν καὶ κατανοοῦντος πτελέαν καὶ ἄμπελον καὶ διακρίνοντος περὶ αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν, φανεροῦταί μοι ὁ ποιμὴν καὶ λέγει: Τί σὺ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ζητεῖς περὶ τῆς πτελέας καὶ τῆς ἀμπέλου; Συζητῶ, φημί, κύριε, ὅτι εὐπρεπέσταταί εἰσιν ἀλλήλαις.
Ταῦτα τὰ δύο δένδρα, φησίν, εἰς τύπον κεῖνται τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ θεοῦ. Ἤθελον, φημί, γνῶναι τὸν τύπον τῶν δένδρων τούτων ὧν λέγεις. Βλέπεις, φησί, τὴν πτελέαν καὶ τὴν ἄμπελον; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε.
Ἡ ἄμπελος, φησίν, αὕτη καρπὸν φέρει, ἡ δὲ πτελέα ξύλον ἄκαρπόν ἐστιν: ἀλλ’ ἡ ἄμπελος αὕτη ἐὰν μὴ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν πτελέαν, οὐ δύναται καρποφορῆσαι πολὺ ἐρριμμένη χαμαί, καὶ ὃν φέρει καρπόν, σεσηπότα φέρει μὴ κρεμαμένη ἐπὶ τῆς πτελέας, ὅταν οὖν ἐπιρριφῇ ἡ ἄμπελος ἐπὶ τὴν πτελέαν, καὶ παῤ ἑαυτῆς φέρει καρπὸν καὶ παρὰ τῆς πτελέας.
βλέπεις οὖν, ὅτι καὶ ἡ πτελέα πολὺν καρπὸν δίδωσιν, οὐκ ἐλάσσονα τῆς ἀμπέλου, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ πλείονα. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, πλείονα; Ὅτι, φησίν, ἡ ἄμπελος κρεμαμένη ἐπὶ τὴν πτελέαν τὸν καρπὸν πολὺν καὶ καλὸν δίδωσιν, ἐρριμμένη δὲ χαμαὶ ὀλίγον καὶ σαπρὸν φέρει. αὕτη οὖν ἡ παραβολὴ εἰς τοὺς δούλους τοῦ θεοῦ κεῖται, εἰς πτωχὸν καὶ πλούσιον.
Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, γνώρισον μοι. Ἄκουε, φησίν: ὁ μὲν πλούσιος ἔχει χρήματα, τὰ δὲ πρὸς τὸν κύριον πτωχεύει, περισπώμενος περὶ τὸν πλοῦτον ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ λίαν μικρὰν ἔχει τὴν ἔντευξιν καὶ τὴν ἐξομολόγησιν πρὸς τὸν κύριον, καὶ ἣν ἔχει, βληχρὰν καὶ μικρὰν καὶ ἄλλην μὴ ἔχουσαν δύναμιν. ὅταν οὖν ἐπαναπάῃ ἐπὶ τὸν πένητα ὁ πλούσιος καὶ χορηγήσῃ αὐτῷ τὰ δέοντα, πιστεύει, ὅτι ἐὰν ἐργάσηται εἰς τὸν πένητα δυνηθήσεται τὸν μισθὸν εὑρεῖν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ: ὅτι ὁ πένης πλούσιός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ ἐντεύξει καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐξομολογήσει καὶ δύναμιν μεγάλην ἔχει παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ἡ ἔντευξις αὐτοῦ. ἐπιχορηγεῖ οὖν ὁ πλούσιος τῷ πένητι πάντα ἀδιστάκτως.
ὁ πένης δὲ ἐπιχορηγούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ πλουσίου ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ, ὑπὲρ τοῦ διδόντος αὐτῷ: κἀκεῖνος ἔτι ἐπισπουδάζει περὶ τοῦ πένητος, ἵνα ἀδιάλειπτος γένηται ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ: οἶδε γάρ, ὅτι ἡ τοῦ πένητος ἔντευξις προσδεκτή ἐστι καὶ πλουσία πρὸς κύριον.
ἀμφότεροι οὖν τὸ ἔργον τελοῦσιν: ὁ μὲν πένης ἐργάζεται τῇ ἐντεύξει, ἐν ᾗ πλουτεῖ, ἣν ἔλαβεν παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου: ταύτην ἀποδίδωσι τῷ κυρίῳ τῷ ἐπιχορηγοῦντι αὐτῷ. καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ὡσαύτως τὸ πλοῦτος, ὃ ἔλαβεν παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ἀδιστάκτως παρέχεται τῷ πένητι. καὶ τοῦτο ἔργον μέγα ἐστὶ καὶ δεκτὸν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ, ὅτι συνῆκεν ἐπὶ τῷ πλούτῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰργάσατο εἰς τὸν πένητα ἐκ τῶν δωρημάτων τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἐτέλεσε τὴν διακονίαν ὀρθῶς.
παρὰ τοῖς οὖν ἀνθρώποις ἡ πτελέα δοκεῖ καρπὸν μὴ φέρειν, καὶ οὐκ οἴδασιν οὐδὲ νοοῦσιν, ὅτι, ὅταν ἀβροχία γένηται, ἡ πτελέα ἔχουσα ὕδωρ τρέφει τὴν ἄμπελον καὶ ἡ ἄμπελος ἀδιάλειπτον ἔχουσα τὸ ὕδωρ διπλοῦν τὸν καρπὸν ἀποδίδωσι, καὶ ὑπὲρ ἑαυτῆς καὶ ὑπὲρ τῆς πτελέας. οὕτως καὶ οἱ πένητες ὑπὲρ τῶν πλουσίων ἐντυγχάνοντες πρὸς τὸν κύριον πληροφοροῦσι τὸ πλοῦτος αὐτῶν, καὶ πάλιν οἱ πλούσιοι χορηγοῦντες τοῖς πένησι τὰ δέοντα πληροφοροῦσι τὰς εὐχὰς αὐτῶν.
γίνονται οὖν ἀμφότεροι κοινωνοὶ τοῦ ἔργου τοῦ δικαίου. ταῦτα οὖν ὁ ποιῶν οὐκ ἐγκαταλειφθήσεται ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἔσται γεγραμμένος εἰς τὰς βίβλους τῶν ζώντων.
μακάριοι οἱ ἔχοντες καὶ συνιέντες, ὅτι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου πλουτίζονται, ὁ γὰρ συνίων τοῦτο δυνήσεται καὶ διακονῆσαί τι ἀγαθόν.
thought_title: The parable of the elm and the vine
orientation: Farmers of the time trained their vines to climb elm trees. The Shepherd makes this a parable of how the rich and the poor help each other before God.
pass_a_gloss: While I was walking into the field and observing an elm and a vine and distinguishing about them and their fruits, the shepherd appears to me and says: What are you seeking in yourself about the elm and the vine? I am examining, I say, lord, because they are most beautiful to each other. These two trees, he says, lie as a type for the servants of God. I wanted, I say, to know the type of these trees which you speak of. Do you see, he says, the elm and the vine? I see, I say, lord. The vine, he says, this one bears fruit, but the elm is a fruitless wood; but this vine, if it does not climb up onto the elm, cannot bear much fruit, thrown on the ground, and the fruit which it bears, it bears rotten, not hanging on the elm. When therefore the vine is thrown upon the elm, it bears fruit both from itself and from the elm. You see therefore that the elm also gives much fruit, not less than the vine, but rather even more. How, I say, lord, more? Because, he says, the vine hanging on the elm gives much and good fruit, but thrown on the ground it bears little and rotten. This parable therefore lies for the servants of God, for poor and rich. How, I say, lord, make it known to me. Listen, he says: the rich man has money, but toward the Lord he is poor, being distracted about his wealth, and he has very small intercession and confession toward the Lord, and what he has is weak and small and having no other power. When therefore the rich man rests upon the poor man and supplies to him the things that are needed, he believes that if he works for the poor man he will be able to find the reward with God; because the poor man is rich in intercession and in confession, and his intercession has great power with God. The rich man therefore supplies to the poor man all things without hesitation. The poor man, being supplied by the rich man, intercedes with God, thanking him, on behalf of the one giving to him; and that one still strives earnestly about the poor man, so that he may be unceasing in his life; for he knows that the intercession of the poor man is acceptable and rich toward the Lord. Both therefore complete the work: the poor man works in intercession, in which he is rich, which he received from the Lord; this he gives back to the Lord who supplies him. And the rich man likewise provides the wealth, which he received from the Lord, without hesitation to the poor man. And this is a great work and acceptable with God, because he understood about his wealth and worked for the poor man from the gifts of the Lord and completed the ministry rightly. Among men therefore the elm seems not to bear fruit, and they do not know nor understand that, when drought occurs, the elm having water nourishes the vine, and the vine having unceasing water gives back double fruit, both for itself and for the elm. So also the poor, interceding for the rich toward the Lord, fulfill their wealth, and again the rich, supplying to the poor the things that are needed, fulfill their prayers. Both therefore become sharers of the work of the righteous. The one therefore doing these things will not be abandoned by God, but will be written in the books of the living. Blessed are those who have and understand that they are made rich by the Lord; for the one understanding this will be able also to minister something good.

choices.why: The verb κεῖνται means 'lie' or 'are set' and τύπον is 'type' or 'pattern'; the literal sense is that the trees are placed as a type for the servants of God.
The verb ἐπαναπαύομαι means 'to rest upon' or 'lean upon'; the rich man rests upon the poor man in the sense of relying on him.
ἔντευξις means 'intercession' or 'petition'; the poor man's prayer to God on behalf of the rich man is the key action.
ἐξομολόγησις means 'confession' or 'acknowledgment'; paired with intercession as the poor man's spiritual wealth.
The adverb means 'without doubting' or 'without hesitation'; the rich man gives to the poor without wavering.
πληροφορέω means 'to fulfill' or 'complete'; the poor fulfill the wealth of the rich through intercession, and the rich fulfill the prayers of the poor through supply.

bible_refs.note: ἔσται γεγραμμένος εἰς τὰς βίβλους τῶν ζώντων

pass_b_english: I was walking in the country, and I noticed an elm and a vine. I was considering them and their fruits when the Shepherd appeared to me. He said, “What are you turning over in your mind about the elm and the vine?” “Sir,” I said, “I am thinking how well they suit each other.”

“These two trees,” he said, “are set as a pattern for the servants of God.” “I would like to know,” I said, “the pattern of these trees you speak of.” “Do you see the elm and the vine?” he asked. “I see them, sir,” I said.

“This vine bears fruit,” he said, “but the elm is a tree without fruit. Yet unless this vine climbs up the elm, it lies cast on the ground and cannot bear much fruit. And the fruit it does bear is rotten, because it does not hang on the elm. So when the vine is cast upon the elm, it bears fruit both from itself and from the elm.

“So you see that the elm too gives much fruit, no less than the vine, and indeed even more.” “How does it give more, sir?” I asked. “Because,” he said, “when the vine hangs on the elm, it gives its fruit in plenty, and the fruit is good. But when it lies cast on the ground, it bears little, and that little is rotten. So this parable is set for the servants of God, for the poor man and the rich.”

“How so, sir?” I said. “Make it known to me.” “Listen,” he said. “The rich man has money, but in the things of the Lord he is poor, for his wealth distracts him. His intercession and his confession toward the Lord are very small. What he has is feeble and small, and has no other power.

“So when the rich man leans on the poor man and supplies him with what he needs, he believes that if he works for the poor man, he will be able to find his reward with God. For the poor man is rich in intercession and in confession, and his intercession has great power with God. So the rich man supplies the poor man with everything, without hesitation.

“And the poor man, supplied by the rich man, intercedes with God and gives him thanks for the one who gives to him. Then the rich man is still more zealous for the poor man, so that the poor man may be supplied without a break all his life. For he knows that the poor man’s intercession is acceptable and rich before the Lord.

“So both complete the work. The poor man works by his intercession, in which he is rich, and which he received from the Lord. He gives it back to the Lord who supplies him. And the rich man likewise, without hesitation, provides the poor man with the wealth that he received from the Lord. This is a great work, and acceptable with God. For the rich man has understood about his wealth, and has worked for the poor man out of the gifts of the Lord, and has carried out his ministry rightly.

“Now people suppose that the elm bears no fruit. They do not know, and they do not grasp, that when a drought comes, the elm holds water and feeds the vine. And the vine, having water without a break, gives double the fruit, both for itself and for the elm. So too the poor, by interceding with the Lord for the rich, make their wealth complete. And the rich in turn, by supplying the poor with what they need, make their prayers complete.
“So both become partners in the righteous work. Whoever does these things will not be forsaken by God, but will be written in the books of the living.
“Blessed are those who have possessions, and who understand that they are made rich by the Lord. For whoever understands this will also be able to carry out some good ministry.”

problems.why: Psalm 69:28 LXX says 'βίβλος ζώντων' (book of the living); 'books of the living' better matches e.g. Luke 10:20 or Phil 4:3.
problems.ruling: Greek says plural 'βίβλους τῶν ζώντων'; Psalm 69:28 LXX has singular 'βίβλος τῶν ζώντων', so citation is inaccurate

problems.why: The source does not cite Luke 10:20; the parenthetical scripture reference is an unwarranted addition.

fixed: Removed the unwarranted parenthetical scripture reference (Luke 10:20); the source simply says 'the books of the living'.

last_rejected.quote: The poor man, being supplied by the rich man, intercedes with God, thanking him for the one who gives to him.
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ πένης δὲ ἐπιχορηγούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ πλουσίου ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ, ὑπὲρ τοῦ διδόντος αὐτῷ
last_rejected.why: Greek says the poor thanks God; English adds that he intercedes with God, changing agency.
last_rejected.fix: The poor man, being supplied by the rich man, thanks God for the one who gives to him.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ means 'intercedes with God'; εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ = 'thanking him.' No agency change; translation accurately renders both verbs.

last_rejected.quote: the poor, interceding for the rich before the Lord, fulfill their wealth, and again the rich, supplying the poor with what they need, fulfill their prayers.
last_rejected.source_quote: οὕτως καὶ οἱ πένητες ὑπὲρ τῶν πλουσίων ἐντυγχάνοντες πρὸς τὸν κύριον πληροφοροῦσι τὸ πλοῦτος αὐτῶν, καὶ πάλιν οἱ πλούσιοι χορηγοῦντες τοῖς πένησι τὰ δέοντα πληροφοροῦσι τὰς εὐχὰς αὐῶν
last_rejected.why: Greek says the poor bring the rich’s wealth before the Lord and the rich supply the poor’s needs, not that they “fulfill” or “intercede”. The English misrepresents the action.
last_rejected.fix: Thus the poor bring the rich’s wealth before the Lord, and the rich, supplying the poor with what is needed, fulfill their prayers.
last_rejected.ruling: πληροφοροῦσι means 'fulfill/bring to fulfillment'; ὑπὲρ τῶν πλουσίων ἐντυγχάνοντες = 'interceding for the rich.' English correctly renders both verbs and objects.
